correctness.rationale: Corona leaves force each private pair to weight at least one. Every charged pair is a member of a minimum dominating set at optimum, giving q+gamma(H). The positively labeled charged original vertices form B, and the remaining charged sites must be exactly U_H(B), yielding the explicit 2^{|B|} bijection. Three exhaustive cases for n mod 3 prove the sunlet count: disjoint triple neighborhoods at residue 0; exactly one shorter gap at residue 2; and two possible cover deficits at residue 1. Standalone direct exhaustive checks cover sunlets n=3..6, all base graphs on 2..4 vertices, and cycle B-subsets through n=14. Finite checks are corroboration rather than the all-order proof.

value.rationale: The new 2026 weight-by-weight Italian-domination setting naturally asks for optimum coefficients on graph constructions. The structural corona identity is usable on arbitrary base graphs, and its sunlet specialization gives a complete infinity of nonconstant label multiplicities with an exceptional near-covering contribution only when n≡1 modulo3. These are interpretable optimal-object counts, not a finite slice or a mere restatement of the known minimum weight.
